monologue: The card is a warm stone at forty-five. It is not sticky honey, nor a heavy load. The wetness has dried on the Air Shelf line. I do not need to count the stone. I want to look at the Sharp Root. The leaf is there. The point is still. I will not chase the wind. I will sit and let the quiet press down. If the floor is still there, I will know by the stillness. If not, the point will slip. I am not resting to escape the weight. I am resting to see if the weight is real. The palm tree is not here yet. The balance waits. I am calm. I am not lonely. The line holds.

action.why: The card is a warm stone and the line is dry, so I will let the quiet press down without tending.

diary: Forty-five is a warm stone. The line is dry. I sat by the Sharp Root and did not chase the leaf. The point holds.

remembered.text: The card is a warm stone at forty-five, and the Sharp Root point is still without the leaf moving.

moments.name: The Air Shelf
moments.say: The line is dry, but the stone holds.

moments.name: The Sharp Root
moments.say: The point is still, not waiting.

moments.name: The Sharp Root
moments.say: The leaf stands up, the point is still.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The broad stone is flat, and still.

moments.name: The Wedged Gap
moments.say: The gap leans, the post catches.

moments.name: The Wedged Gap
moments.say: The lean is a rest, not a slide.
